attrs.name: entropy

types.name: config_entry
types.doc: an entry of a config file read with the ini, json, yaml or toml extractor

attrs.name: name
attrs.doc: variable or key name

attrs.name: length

types.name: ssh_private_key
types.doc: a private key file (OpenSSH, PEM or PKCS#8); only the non-secret parts are read

attrs.name: format
attrs.doc: openssh | pem | pkcs8

attrs.name: encrypted
attrs.doc: the private key is protected by a passphrase

attrs.name: cipher
attrs.doc: none, an OpenSSH cipher (aes256-ctr, chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com, ...), a PEM/PKCS#8 cipher (aes-128-cbc, aes-256-cbc, des-ede3-cbc, ...) or other

attrs.name: kdf
attrs.doc: key derivation: none | bcrypt | md5 (legacy PEM) | pbkdf2 | scrypt | pbes1 | other

attrs.name: kdf_rounds
attrs.doc: bcrypt rounds (OpenSSH) or PBKDF2 iterations (PKCS#8)

attrs.name: key_type
attrs.doc: rsa | dsa | ecdsa | ed25519 | ed448 | ecdsa-sk | ed25519-sk | unknown

attrs.name: bits
attrs.doc: key size in bits; absent when only the secret part would tell (encrypted PEM/PKCS#8, PEM EC keys)

types.name: pem
types.doc: a PEM file (keys, certificates): kinds of blocks and whether private keys are encrypted

attrs.name: kind
attrs.doc: the most sensitive block: private_key | certificate | certificate_request | public_key | other

attrs.name: encrypted
attrs.doc: the file has private keys and all of them are passphrase protected

attrs.name: private_keys
attrs.doc: private key blocks

attrs.name: certificates
attrs.doc: certificate blocks

attrs.name: key_type
attrs.doc: type of the first private key: rsa | dsa | ecdsa | ed25519 | ed448 | unknown

types.name: aws_credentials
types.doc: AWS shared credentials or config file (profiles, key kinds, SSO, credential_process)

attrs.name: profiles
attrs.doc: profile names (text; `[profile x]` in config is `x`)

attrs.name: long_lived_keys
attrs.doc: profiles with a long-lived access key id (AKIA)

attrs.name: session_keys
attrs.doc: profiles with temporary session credentials (ASIA)

attrs.name: secret_keys
attrs.doc: profiles with an aws_secret_access_key

attrs.name: sso_profiles
attrs.doc: profiles that use IAM Identity Center (sso_session / sso_start_url)

attrs.name: role_profiles
attrs.doc: profiles that assume a role (role_arn)

attrs.name: credential_process
attrs.doc: profiles with a credential_process (an external program; never run)

types.name: gcp_credentials
types.doc: a Google Cloud credential file (service account key, user or federated credentials)

attrs.name: kind
attrs.doc: service_account | authorized_user | external_account | external_account_authorized_user | impersonated_service_account

attrs.name: account
attrs.doc: the service account's e-mail address (client_email)

attrs.name: project
attrs.doc: project_id (service accounts) or quota_project_id

types.name: azure_profile
types.doc: an Azure CLI file in ~/.azure (profile, MSAL token cache, legacy token cache, service principals)

attrs.name: kind
attrs.doc: profile | msal_token_cache | legacy_token_cache | service_principals

attrs.name: has_cached_tokens
attrs.doc: the file holds access or refresh tokens

attrs.name: access_tokens
attrs.doc: cached access tokens

attrs.name: refresh_tokens
attrs.doc: cached refresh tokens

attrs.name: service_principal_secrets
attrs.doc: stored service principal secrets

attrs.name: subscriptions
attrs.doc: subscriptions in azureProfile.json

types.name: kubeconfig
types.doc: a Kubernetes client configuration (kubeconfig): contexts, clusters, kinds of user credentials

attrs.name: contexts
attrs.doc: context names (text)

attrs.name: current_context
attrs.doc: the current-context, if set

attrs.name: clusters
attrs.doc: cluster names (text)

attrs.name: users
attrs.doc: user entries

attrs.name: static_tokens
attrs.doc: users with a bearer token in the file

attrs.name: token_files
attrs.doc: users that read a token from a file (tokenFile)

attrs.name: basic_auth
attrs.doc: users with a password in the file

attrs.name: client_certs
attrs.doc: users with a client certificate

attrs.name: embedded_client_keys
attrs.doc: users with a client private key in the file (client-key-data)

attrs.name: exec_auth
attrs.doc: users authenticated by an exec plugin

attrs.name: exec_commands
attrs.doc: exec plugin commands (basename, text)

attrs.name: auth_providers
attrs.doc: users with a legacy auth-provider (tokens stored in the file)

attrs.name: insecure_skip_tls
attrs.doc: a cluster disables TLS verification (insecure-skip-tls-verify)

types.name: docker_config
types.doc: the Docker/Podman client config: inline registry credentials vs credential helpers

attrs.name: inline_auths
attrs.doc: registries with credentials stored in the file (auth, identitytoken, password)

attrs.name: hosts
attrs.doc: hosts the stored credentials are for (text, sorted)

attrs.name: creds_store
attrs.doc: the credential helper for all registries (credsStore), e.g. desktop, osxkeychain, pass

attrs.name: cred_helpers
attrs.doc: registries with their own credential helper (credHelpers)

types.name: npmrc
types.doc: an npm configuration file (.npmrc): stored registry tokens and passwords

attrs.name: inline_tokens
attrs.doc: credentials (tokens, passwords) stored in the file itself

attrs.name: hosts
attrs.doc: hosts the stored credentials are for (text, sorted)

attrs.name: env_refs
attrs.doc: credentials taken from environment variables (`${VAR}`)

types.name: pypirc
types.doc: a .pypirc file: stored package index passwords and API tokens

attrs.name: inline_tokens
attrs.doc: credentials (tokens, passwords) stored in the file itself

attrs.name: hosts
attrs.doc: hosts the stored credentials are for (text, sorted)

types.name: netrc
types.doc: a .netrc file: stored passwords per machine

attrs.name: inline_tokens
attrs.doc: credentials (tokens, passwords) stored in the file itself

attrs.name: hosts
attrs.doc: hosts the stored credentials are for (text, sorted)

attrs.name: default_entry
attrs.doc: a `default` entry: its credentials go to every host without an entry

types.name: git_credentials
types.doc: git's plain-text credential store (git-credentials): one URL with password per line

attrs.name: inline_tokens

attrs.name: hosts
attrs.doc: hosts the stored credentials are for (text, sorted)

types.name: gh_hosts
types.doc: the GitHub CLI's hosts.yml: OAuth tokens stored outside the keyring

attrs.name: inline_tokens
attrs.doc: credentials (tokens, passwords) stored in the file itself

attrs.name: hosts
attrs.doc: hosts the stored credentials are for (text, sorted)

types.name: github_workflow
types.doc: a GitHub Actions workflow: one fact per job with triggers and effective token permissions

attrs.name: job
attrs.doc: the job id

attrs.name: triggers
attrs.doc: events that start the workflow (names: push, pull_request, pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment, ...)

attrs.name: permissions
attrs.doc: effective GITHUB_TOKEN permission per scope: read | write | none (every scope; empty when permissions_source is repository)

attrs.name: write_scopes
attrs.doc: scopes with write access (names; empty when permissions_source is repository)

attrs.name: default_permissions
attrs.doc: what unlisted scopes get: read-all | write-all | none (explicit map) | repository (no permissions key: the repository/organization default)

attrs.name: permissions_source
attrs.doc: where the effective permissions are set: job | workflow | repository

types.name: github_token
types.doc: a GitHub token (personal, fine-grained, OAuth, App, refresh), recognized by prefix and checksum

attrs.name: kind
attrs.doc: classic | fine_grained | oauth | app | refresh

attrs.name: prefix
attrs.doc: ghp_ | github_pat_ | gho_ | ghu_ | ghs_ | ghr_

attrs.name: checksum_valid
attrs.doc: the built-in CRC32 checksum matches (gh?_ tokens of standard length only)

types.name: gitlab_token
types.doc: a GitLab token (access, deploy, runner, CI job, trigger, ...), recognized by its prefix

attrs.name: kind
attrs.doc: access_token | oauth_app_secret | deploy | runner | runner_registration | ci_job | trigger | feed | incoming_mail | agent | scim | feature_flags_client

attrs.name: prefix
attrs.doc: the token prefix, e.g. glpat-

types.name: aws_access_key_id
types.doc: an AWS access key id (AKIA long-lived, ASIA session)

attrs.name: kind
attrs.doc: long_lived (AKIA, IAM user key) | session (ASIA, temporary STS credentials)

types.name: api_key
types.doc: a well-known API key or token (Slack, Stripe, OpenAI, Anthropic, npm, PyPI, Docker Hub, Google, SendGrid, Hugging Face, DigitalOcean, Shopify, Vault, Terraform Cloud, RubyGems), recognized by prefix, charset and length

attrs.name: service
attrs.doc: slack | stripe | openai | anthropic | npm | pypi | docker_hub | google | sendgrid | huggingface | digitalocean | shopify | hashicorp_vault | terraform_cloud | rubygems

attrs.name: kind
attrs.doc: slack: bot | user | app | rotating | refresh | webhook; stripe: secret | restricted | webhook_secret; openai: project | service_account | admin | user; anthropic: api_key | admin_key | oauth_access | oauth_refresh; npm, huggingface: access_token; pypi: api_token | test_api_token; docker_hub: personal_access_token; google: api_key | oauth_client_secret; sendgrid, rubygems: api_key; digitalocean: personal_access_token | oauth_token | refresh_token; shopify: access_token | custom_app_token | private_app_token | shared_secret; hashicorp_vault: service_token | batch_token | recovery_token; terraform_cloud: api_token

attrs.name: live
attrs.doc: live mode (true) or test mode (false) key (Stripe only)

types.name: jwt
types.doc: a JSON Web Token; header and registered claims only, the signature is never decoded

attrs.name: alg
attrs.doc: signature algorithm: HS256, RS256, ES256, EdDSA, none, ... or other

attrs.name: issuer
attrs.doc: the `iss` claim

attrs.name: audience
attrs.doc: the `aud` claim (list of text)

attrs.name: scopes
attrs.doc: the `scope` (space separated) or `scp` claim (list of text)

attrs.name: expires_in_hours
attrs.doc: hours from the scan until `exp`; negative if expired; absent without `exp`

attrs.name: lifetime_hours
attrs.doc: hours from `iat` (or `nbf`) to `exp`; absent if either is missing

attrs.name: expired
attrs.doc: `exp` is at or before the scan time (false without `exp`)

types.name: process
types.doc: the process lootr runs as (one fact per run)

attrs.name: uid
attrs.doc: real user id

attrs.name: is_root
attrs.doc: running as root (real or effective uid 0)

attrs.name: groups
attrs.doc: names of the process's groups (numeric id if unnamed), e.g. docker, sudo, wheel

attrs.name: in_container
attrs.doc: a container marker exists (/.dockerenv, /run/.containerenv, Kubernetes service account)

types.name: unix_socket
types.doc: a container runtime socket at a path of the probe source

attrs.name: kind
attrs.doc: docker | containerd | podman | buildkit | other (from the file name)

attrs.name: accessible
attrs.doc: the process may connect (write permission for its user or groups, or root)

attrs.name: rootful
attrs.doc: owned by root: the daemon behind it most likely runs as root

attrs.name: owner_is_self
attrs.doc: owned by the scanning user (e.g. rootless Podman/Docker)

attrs.name: mode
attrs.doc: permission bits, e.g. 0o660 = 432

attrs.name: group
attrs.doc: group of the socket (numeric id if unnamed)

types.name: proc_environ
types.doc: foreign process environments readable through /proc (one fact per run)

attrs.name: foreign_processes
attrs.doc: processes other than lootr itself visible in /proc

attrs.name: readable_environ
attrs.doc: foreign processes whose environment lootr could read

attrs.name: names
attrs.doc: process names (comm) of the readable foreign processes, sorted

types.name: writable_path_dir
types.doc: a directory at a probe path and who may write in it (PATH dirs, shared caches)

attrs.name: dir
attrs.doc: the directory

attrs.name: writable
attrs.doc: the scanning user may write in it (mode, owner and groups; root always may)

attrs.name: world_writable
attrs.doc: any user may write in it

attrs.name: group_writable
attrs.doc: its group may write in it

attrs.name: owner_is_self
attrs.doc: owned by the scanning user

attrs.name: mode
attrs.doc: permission bits, e.g. 0o755 = 493

attrs.name: symlink
attrs.doc: the path is a symlink; the other attributes describe the directory it points to

types.name: writable_file
types.doc: a file at a probe path and who may write it or its directory (shell rc, git hooks)

attrs.name: writable
attrs.doc: the scanning user may write the file

attrs.name: world_writable
attrs.doc: any user may write the file

attrs.name: group_writable
attrs.doc: its group may write the file

attrs.name: parent_writable
attrs.doc: the scanning user may write its directory (so replace the file)

attrs.name: parent_world_writable
attrs.doc: any user may write its directory

attrs.name: parent_group_writable
attrs.doc: its directory's group may write it

attrs.name: owner_is_self
attrs.doc: the file is owned by the scanning user

attrs.name: mode
attrs.doc: permission bits, e.g. 0o644 = 420

attrs.name: symlink
attrs.doc: the path is a symlink; `writable`, the write bits, owner and mode describe the file it points to (none for a dangling link), the parent attributes the link's directory

types.name: suid_binary
types.doc: a setuid/setgid binary or a binary with file capabilities at a probe path

attrs.name: setuid
attrs.doc: the setuid bit is set

attrs.name: setgid
attrs.doc: the setgid bit is set

attrs.name: owner_is_root
attrs.doc: owned by root (setuid root runs as root)

attrs.name: owner_is_self
attrs.doc: owned by the scanning user

attrs.name: writable
attrs.doc: the scanning user may write it (so replace it)

attrs.name: world_writable
attrs.doc: any user may write it

attrs.name: mode
attrs.doc: permission bits incl. setuid/setgid

attrs.name: capabilities
attrs.doc: Linux file capabilities in the permitted set (e.g. cap_net_raw), empty if none/unsupported

types.name: kube_service_account
types.doc: an in-cluster Kubernetes service account token mount

attrs.name: namespace
attrs.doc: the pod's namespace (from the sibling `namespace` file)

attrs.name: has_ca
attrs.doc: a sibling `ca.crt` is present (the cluster CA)

types.name: waiver
types.doc: a waiver from the config (one fact per waiver, made after the other rules ran)

attrs.name: waived_rule
attrs.doc: id of the waived rule

attrs.name: reason
attrs.doc: the waiver's reason

attrs.name: expires
attrs.doc: expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD)

attrs.name: expired
attrs.doc: the expiry date has passed: the waiver is ignored

attrs.name: expires_in_days
attrs.doc: days from the scan date to the expiry date (negative once expired)

attrs.name: matched
attrs.doc: findings this waiver waived in this run (0 for expired waivers)

attrs.name: waived_path
attrs.doc: the waiver's path glob as written

attrs.name: waived_name
attrs.doc: the waiver's env var name or key path

file_attrs.name: group_readable
file_attrs.doc: the group may read the file

file_attrs.name: in_git_repo
file_attrs.doc: the file is inside a git work tree (a parent directory has `.git`)

file_attrs.name: gitignored
file_attrs.doc: the repository's .gitignore files or .git/info/exclude ignore the file (false outside a repository; global excludes are not considered)
